name: Can I live in my house while building an ADU in the backyard, or will construction be too disruptive?

mainEntity.name: Can I live in my house while building an ADU in the backyard, or will construction be too disruptive?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Most homeowners **do stay in their main house** while a backyard ADU is being built, accepting several months of noise, dust, and workers on site. It’s disruptive but usually manageable with clear boundaries.

Because the ADU is separate from the main dwelling, contractors can often stage work and materials outside your living area. The biggest impacts are access through side yards and occasional utility shutdowns.

Key factors:
- Site access: width of side yards and impact on privacy
- Construction hours allowed by local noise ordinances
- Temporary power/water interruptions during utility tie‑ins
- Safety and security around open excavations and materials

Discuss logistics with your builder before work starts: where crews park, hours of work, and how they’ll secure the site each night. Plan ahead for a few days of extra disruption during major utility connections.

Seasoned ADU contractors are used to working on occupied properties and can minimize intrusion with good planning.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, most people live in the main house while the ADU is built, though you’ll deal with months of noise, dust, and people in your yard. Clear rules about work hours, site access, parking, and safety—plus planning for brief utility shutoffs—make the experience much more manageable.
